title: Coelom and Metamerism Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
After the rain, Diya watches an earthworm crawl out, its body a long chain of rings. Are the rings only on the outside? And what is inside, between the skin and the gut?

You will see the body as a tube inside a tube, then a zoom ladder into the earthworm: its segments, a lengthwise cut with walls and repeated organs, and a cross-section showing the coelom lined by mesoderm. We sort animals into coelomates, pseudocoelomates (mesoderm in scattered pouches) and acoelomates with NCERT examples, watch metamerism and a crawling wave of muscles, and place the notochord. Then the earthworm and Ascaris side by side, a worked example sorting three cross-sections, the exam trap about body cavities, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 34 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Rings on an earthworm
0:34 A tube inside a tube
0:49 Zoom ladder into the earthworm
1:20 Coelomate, pseudocoelomate, acoelomate
2:15 Segmentation and metamerism
2:41 The notochord: chordates and non-chordates
3:10 True vs false coelom + pause and think
3:46 Worked example: three cross-sections
4:22 Exam trap: is every cavity a coelom?
4:46 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:19 Recap and three questions to answer
